Rules summary Contents 1 Friendly Fishing 1.1 Overview 1.2 Components 1.3 Setup 1.3.1 1. Choose the Board Side 1.3.2 2. Prepare the Tiles 1.3.3 3. Place the Boat 1.3.4 4. Choose the First Player 1.4 Gameplay 1.5 Move the Boat 1.6 Collect the Tile 1.7 Returning to the Central Island 1.8 Central Island 1.9 Action Tiles 1.9.1 Swap 2 Fish 1.9.2 Swap 2 Tiles 1.9.3 Slide a Tile 1.9.4 Remove a Tile 1.9.5 Double Points 1.10 Basic Fish Tiles 1.11 Common Fish 1.12 Crayfish 1.13 Special Fish Tiles 1.14 Kingfish 1.15 Lunkers 1.16 Dinkers 1.17 Skipjacks 1.18 Shiners 1.19 Junk 1.20 Game End 1.20.1 Skipjack Reminder 1.21 Final Scoring 1.22 Fishing Score 1.22.1 2-Player Game 1.23 Final Score: 3–5 Players 1.24 Ties 1.25 Scoring Summary 1.26 Clarifications 1.27 Strategy Tips 1.28 Credits Friendly Fishing Overview Friendly Fishing is a semi-cooperative set collection game in which all players share the same fishing boat. On your turn: Move the boat to a new tile. Collect the tile you land on. Try to leave good opportunities for the next player. There is one important twist: In a 3–5 player game, your final score is your own Fishing Score plus the Fishing Score of the player on your left . The game ends when the boat can no longer move. Components 1 Double-Sided Game Board 1 Boat Token 31 Basic Fish Tiles 18 Special Fish Tiles 6 sets of 3 5 Action Tiles 1 of each type Setup 1. Choose the Board Side Place the Game Board in the center of the table. For a 5-player game : Use the side with the Large Central Island . For other player counts: Use the Small Central Island for a shorter game. Use the Large Central Island for a longer game. 2. Prepare the Tiles Choose Special Fish sets based on the board side: Board Side Special Fish Sets Special Fish Tiles Small Central Island 2 sets 6 Large Central Island 4 sets 12 Add the chosen Special Fish Tiles to: All 31 Basic Fish Tiles All 5 Action Tiles Mix all tiles face-down. Place them randomly on the water spaces of the board. 3. Place the Boat Place the Boat Token on the Central Island. 4. Choose the First Player Choose any starting player. For example: The player who most recently went fishing may go first. Gameplay Players take turns moving the shared Boat Token and collecting tiles. On your turn: Move the Boat. Collect the Tile. Then play passes to the next player. Move the Boat At the start of your turn: Move the Boat from its current space to a tile in an adjacent water space . Normally, the Boat must move to an adjacent tile. Exception: Skipjacks allow a special non-adjacent move. Collect the Tile After moving onto a tile: Remove it from the board. Place it face-up in front of you. Keep your collected tiles visible so everyone can see how many of each type you have. If you collect an Action Tile: Resolve its effect immediately. Returning to the Central Island If there are no possible moves from the Boat's current space: Return the Boat to the Central Island. Move the Boat from the Central Island to an adjacent tile. This is the only way the Boat may return to the Central Island. Central Island The Central Island counts as one single space . Depending on the board side: Central Island Adjacent Water Spaces Small 8 Large 10 When moving from the Central Island: You may move to any adjacent tile. Action Tiles Action Tiles score 0 points . Whenever you collect one: Resolve it immediately. Swap 2 Fish Take 1 Basic Fish Tile from another player and give them 1 of your Basic Fish Tiles, if possible. Swap 2 Tiles Choose any 2 tiles still on the board. Swap their positions. Slide a Tile Choose 1 tile on the board. Move it to a new space through any number of connected open water spaces. Remove a Tile Choose any 1 tile anywhere on the board. Return it to the box. Double Points Place the Double Points Tile beside one of the colored Common Fish icons in a corner of the board. During final scoring: That Common Fish color is worth double points for every player . Basic Fish Tiles There are two types of Basic Fish: Common Fish Crayfish Common Fish Each Common Fish color scores according to how many fish of that color you collected. Fish of One Color Points 1 1 2 3 3 6 4 10 5 15 6 21 There are 6 fish of each Common Fish color. Remember: The Double Points Action Tile may cause one Common Fish color to score twice its normal value. Crayfish There are 7 Crayfish. The players with the most and second-most Crayfish score: Result Points Most Crayfish 8 Second-Most Crayfish 4 If players tie for either position: All tied players receive the full points for that position. Special Fish Tiles Each Special Fish set contains 3 matching tiles. Only the Special Fish sets chosen during setup are used. Kingfish Instant Win If you collect all 3 Kingfish: You immediately win the game. In a 5-player game: You only need to collect 2 Kingfish . This victory is not shared with another player. Lunkers Only the Last Lunker Scores Whenever you collect a Lunker: Every other player who already has a Lunker must discard it to the box. As a result: Only the most recently collected Lunker remains in play. The remaining Lunker is worth: 5 points Dinkers Dinkers are worth: 2 points each Whenever you move onto a Dinker: You may collect it normally OR Leave the Dinker where it is and immediately move the Boat again. You may only continue moving if another legal move is available from the Dinker's space. Skipjacks Skipjacks are worth: 5 points each Skipjacks provide a special Boat move. You may collect a Skipjack by moving: In a straight line Through any number of connected open water spaces Directly onto the Skipjack You may not move through: Another tile The Central Island Important: This is the only way to move the Boat to a non-adjacent tile. Shiners Shiners score differently depending on how many you collect. Shiners Points 1 -2 2 5 3 12 Collecting only 1 Shiner loses points, but collecting additional Shiners can make them valuable. Junk Each Junk Tile is worth: -3 points Game End At the start of a player's turn, first check whether the Boat has a legal move. If no move is possible: Return the Boat to the Central Island. Check again for a legal move. If the Boat is on the Central Island and still cannot move: The game ends immediately. Skipjack Reminder If Skipjacks are in play: Check whether a legal Skipjack move is available before ending the game. A Skipjack may still be reachable even when no adjacent tile is available. Final Scoring When the game ends, calculate each player's Fishing Score . For games with 3–5 players, also calculate each player's Final Score . Fishing Score Your Fishing Score is the total value of all scoring tiles you collected. Include: Common Fish Crayfish Special Fish Double Points effects Negative points from applicable tiles 2-Player Game In a 2-player game: Compare Fishing Scores directly. The player with the higher Fishing Score wins. Final Score: 3–5 Players In a 3–5 player game: Your Final Score equals: Your Fishing Score + the Fishing Score of the player on your left Example: Your Fishing Score = 21 Left neighbor's Fishing Score = 24 Final Score = 45 The player with the highest Final Score wins. This means helping the player on your left can improve your own final result. Ties If players tie for the highest winning score: They share the victory. Scoring Summary Tile Scoring Common Fish 1 / 3 / 6 / 10 / 15 / 21 points for 1–6 of one color Crayfish 8 for most, 4 for second-most Kingfish Collect all 3 to immediately win; only 2 required with 5 players Lunker Only the last remaining Lunker scores 5 Dinker 2 points each; may leave behind and move again Skipjack 5 points each; special straight-line movement Shiner 1 = -2, 2 = 5, 3 = 12 Junk -3 each Action Tiles 0 points Clarifications The Boat normally moves only to an adjacent tile. The Central Island is one space, regardless of its physical size. The Boat only returns to the Central Island when no legal move exists from its current location. When returning to the Central Island, the active player must continue their turn by moving to an available tile. Skipjacks may provide legal moves that are not adjacent. Action Tiles are resolved immediately when collected. Action Tiles are worth no points. Collected tiles remain face-up and visible to all players. The Double Points Action affects every player during scoring. The Kingfish victory happens immediately and bypasses normal final scoring. Strategy Tips Your own collection is only part of your score in a 3–5 player game. Pay close attention to the player on your left—their Fishing Score contributes directly to yours. Leaving a useful tile available can sometimes benefit you more than collecting the best tile yourself. Action Tiles can dramatically change future movement paths. Be careful when moving tiles near the Central Island; they may affect how long the game lasts. If Skipjacks are in play, remember that seemingly isolated areas may still be reachable. Kingfish can create an immediate threat that may need to be blocked. Credits Game Design: Bruno Faidutti and Alex Randolph Development: Paul Salomon Illustration: Alisha Giroux Graphic Design: Jon Merchant Rulebook & Editing: Jason D. Kingsley Playtesting: Miles Bensky, Valérie Chassé, The Haveman Family, Chris Moase, Darren Neely, Tommy O’Brien, Mark Wisdon, Pete Wissinger, and more

---

A reel and a rod, some friends, and a boat - is there anything more relaxing? Let's spend the day together, fishing this pond. And hey, I'll give you a hand and help you catch that big fish you've been after.

Friendly Fishing is a semi-cooperative set collection game in which players share a fishing boat. On your turn you simply move the boat and claim a fish token. You'll want to set the next player up for a good move, because there's a twist.  At the end of the game, everyone scores the tokens in front of them, but each player's final score is their own fish score, plus their left neighbor's fish score! Most points wins.

Friendly Fishing offers a casual day on the pond with a unique style of player interaction.

-description from publisher
community_text:
[Rating: 5/10] I like what they are going for but feel like it needed to be polished a bit more. There was one game where the skipjack meant that I had zero options and just took the next fish. Whoever had the most fish in the double points color won every time. We also had a game with a tie which meant that two different people also had a time which felt bad. For now, I have to pass on this game.

[Rating: 5.5/10] Adorable game. This will work for a lot of people. I don't particularly enjoy the scoring system of the game, which is why I rate it lower, but others will find it interesting. You score for what you collect and what the player to your left collects as well. You want to set them up, but not so well that they win. It is a fine line to balance. It was interesting, but not what I would be asking to play.

[Rating: 7/10] Friendly Fishing is a neat semi-cooperative game with map reduction tile collection similar to Hey That's My Fish (except you can only travel one adjacent space). Game arc definitely feels more satisfying than its predecessor Tonari because you reset the player piece after a dead end in this one.

[Rating: 7/10] I like fishing games. The combined scores is somewhat uncommon. The play is super simple and I expect this to get played in a lot of situations. Looks nice.

[Rating: 7/10] Friendly Fishing is an enjoyable game that has some tricky shared incentives. You want to set up a good move while not letting that good move set up a good move. In a 3 player game, you can ideally calculate a whole round ahead. It is a fairly relaxed game, but one with a little bit of depth worth the 20 minutes it takes

[Rating: 7.5/10] A pleasant abstract with good presentation, clean simple rules, and excellent flow. Approachable theme, and enjoyable to play. Abstracts are not my preferred genre but I like this one.
